title: Vasquez's own view: God's definition of our acts neither precedes nor follows the will's determination but accompanies it
source_text: XXXV. Itaque ipse aliud excogitat, nempe Definitionem Dei, quae praefinit opera nostra sigillatim, non praecedere ordine causae determinationem nostrae voluntatis, nec etiam illam sequi; sed eam comitari. Unde colligit necessitatem, quae sequitur positionem decreti Dei, non esse antecedentem, sed comitantem nostram libertatem & determinationem: ac proinde libertatem nostram ea necessitate nec impediri, nec laedi: cum libertati praejudicet sola necessitas praecedens: non vero quae libertatem ipsam, vel sequitur, vel comitatur.
pass_a_gloss: XXXV. Therefore he himself devises something else, namely that the Definition of God, which foreordains our works singly, does not precede in order of cause the determination of our will, nor yet follow it; but accompanies it. Whence he gathers that the necessity which follows the positing of the decree of God is not antecedent, but accompanying our freedom and determination: and therefore that our freedom by that necessity is neither impeded, nor hurt: since only preceding necessity prejudices freedom: not truly that which either follows, or accompanies freedom itself.
pass_b_english: So Vasquez devises something else of his own. God's definition, which foreordains our works one by one, neither comes before the determination of our will in the order of causes nor follows it, but accompanies it.

From this he concludes that the necessity which follows once God's decree is posited is not antecedent to our freedom and determination but accompanies them. So our freedom is neither hindered nor harmed by that necessity, since only a preceding necessity damages freedom, not one that follows or accompanies it.

does not precede in order of cause

choices.why: Necessity that precedes and so constrains the act, contrasted with consequent or concomitant necessity; kept as technical terms.
